iss.note: Effective dose on the ISS: about 40 to 90 mSv per six-month mission.

moon.note: Galactic cosmic rays on the lunar surface with optimized shielding: low end at solar maximum, high end at solar minimum.

mars.note: Galactic cosmic rays on the Martian surface (planet and thin atmosphere shield part of the dose): low end at solar maximum, high end at solar minimum.

shelter.text: Radiation alerting gives early warning so the crew can safe the vehicle and configure a shelter. On the ISS, Radi-N2 measured a lower neutron dose in the sleeping quarters than elsewhere on the station.

moon.note: Estimate for the October 1989 solar particle event on the lunar surface with a 10 g/cm2 water-equivalent shield.

mars.note: Estimate for the October 1989 event on the Martian surface: under 25 mSv with a 10 g/cm2 water-equivalent shield, about 40 mSv with only the planet and atmosphere.
